name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
facility: Combustion Integrated Rack, Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus
summary: Burned free-floating fuel droplets to study how flames go out and how well gaseous suppressants work. Best known for finding that large heptane droplets keep burning in an invisible, low-temperature 'cool flame' after the visible flame goes out.

sources.title: Detailed Results From the Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) March 2009 to December 2011 (NASA/TP—2015-216046)

name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment 2
facility: Combustion Integrated Rack, Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus
summary: Follow-on droplet studies: burning of fuel mixtures, soot formation, and how neighbouring droplets and slow airflow change burning and extinction.

name: Cool Flames Investigation
summary: Studies low-temperature 'cool flames' that were discovered in FLEX. Cool flames are hard to see and detect, so they matter for spacecraft fire detection.

name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments
summary: A set of gaseous-flame studies (including Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame, Flame Design, Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames, Electric-Field Effects, and the Burning Rate Emulator) on soot, flame structure and extinction limits.

sources.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME) on the International Space Station (ISS)

name: Burning and Suppression of Solids (I and II)
summary: Burned small solid samples in a slow, controlled airflow to see how flames spread and when they go out, and tested putting them out with nitrogen.

sources.title: Thickness and Fuel Preheating Effects on Material Flammability in Microgravity from the BASS Experiment
sources.locator: Abstract: Microgravity Science Glovebox, air flow up to 40 cm/s

sources.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II (BASS-II) Summary Report

name: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction
summary: A facility for igniting and burning solid materials under controlled oxygen, pressure and airflow, to map when spacecraft materials can ignite and keep burning.

sources.title: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction (SoFIE) Project on ISS
sources.locator: Abstract: insert for the Combustion Integrated Rack

name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment (Saffire I to VI)
facility: Cygnus cargo vehicle, after leaving the ISS
summary: The first large-scale fires in space, lit inside an empty cargo vehicle after it left the station. Measured how flames grow on spacecraft-sized samples and how quickly smoke and heat change the cabin air. No crew on board.

sources.title: The Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire) - Objectives, Development and Status
Preliminary Results from the Saffire VI Experiment
sources.locator: Abstract: last flight, on an orbiting Cygnus

name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment
summary: Measured the size of smoke particles from overheated spacecraft materials in microgravity, to judge how well spacecraft smoke detectors would see them.

sources.title: Particle and Smoke Detection on ISS for Next Generation Smoke Detectors
Particle Morphology and Size Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-2
sources.locator: Abstract: SAME-2 on Expedition 24, July–September 2010; first flight Expedition 15

name: Flammability Limits at Reduced-gravity Experiment
summary: A Japanese study of how gravity changes the oxygen level at which solid materials stop burning, with the aim of improving ground tests for spacecraft materials.

sources.title: NTRS search: FLARE flammability limits reduced gravity

name: Zero Gravity Research Facility (Glenn Research Center)
facility: Vacuum drop shaft, about 5 seconds of free fall
summary: A ground drop tower that gives a few seconds of microgravity, used for decades for quick, repeatable combustion tests before (and instead of) flying to space.

sources.title: NTRS search: Zero Gravity Research Facility combustion

name: 2.2 Second Drop Tower (Glenn Research Center)
facility: Drop tower, about 2.2 seconds of free fall
summary: A shorter, faster-turnaround drop tower used for many early and exploratory microgravity combustion tests.

sources.title: NTRS search: 2.2 second drop tower combustion

name: NASA-STD-6001 material flammability test (Test 1)
facility: Upward flame propagation test, run on the ground
summary: The ground test NASA uses to decide which materials may fly. A key open question for fire safety is how well this 1 g test predicts burning in microgravity and partial gravity.

sources.title: Organizing Questions for Reduced-Gravity Flammability
sources.locator: Abstract: is NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 conservative in reduced gravity?

name: Apollo 1 cabin fire
summary: A fire in a pure-oxygen cabin during a ground test killed three astronauts and reshaped how NASA treats cabin atmosphere and flammable materials. Context, not microgravity data.

sources.title: Apollo 204 Review Board activities: Second interim report

name: Mir oxygen generator fire
facility: Mir space station, solid-fuel oxygen generator
summary: A fire from an oxygen-generating canister filled the station with smoke. The best-known real fire in orbit, and a lesson on detection, smoke and crew response.

sources.title: NTRS search: Mir fire 1997 oxygen generator
